LinkedIn.text:
LINKEDIN CONTENT GUIDELINES

The Modern Business Architect

1. PURPOSE OF LINKEDIN (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

LinkedIn is not where you explain everything.
It is where you signal.

The purpose of LinkedIn content is to:
create recognition ("this feels like me")
introduce tension
challenge lazy thinking
invite conversation without asking for it

LinkedIn is the front door.
Substack is the thinking room.

If a post tries to do both, it fails.

2. ROLE OF LINKEDIN IN THE ECOSYSTEM

LinkedIn exists to:
Surface problems people already feel
Name confusion they cannot articulate
Position you as someone who sees structure where others see noise
Quietly pull the right people closer

This is not content for everyone.
This is content for builders, future builders, and restless minds.

3. FREQUENCY & RHYTHM

Posting Frequency
5-7 posts per week is acceptable
Daily posting is allowed
Silence is better than forced content

Rule:
Short and sharp beats rare and heavy.

Best Days to Post
Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday -> highest signal
Monday -> reflection tone works
Friday -> light or no posting
Weekends -> generally avoid

Best Times to Post
08:00-10:00 AM
12:00-01:00 PM
Avoid evenings and late afternoons.

4. POST TYPES (ROTATE, DON'T REPEAT)
Every LinkedIn post must fit one of these types.
When generating content, the GPT should either ask which type you want or suggest the most appropriate type based on context.

TYPE 1 - Short Signal Post
Frequency: 2-3x/week
Length: 3-6 lines
Purpose: stop the scroll, introduce tension, provoke thought
Characteristics: one idea, one tension, no explanation, no CTA
Example tone: "Most people don't fail at business. They fail at deciding what they're actually building."

TYPE 2 - Medium Reflection Post
Frequency: 2-3x/week
Length: 6-12 lines
Purpose: build familiarity, show how you think, gently reframe assumptions
Characteristics: conversational but precise, grounded in reality, no teaching tone

TYPE 3 - Long Authority Post
Frequency: 1-2x/week max
Length: 15-25 lines
Purpose: demonstrate depth, establish authority, show structure
Characteristics: skimmable, spaced paragraphs, no walls of text, no frameworks as marketing

5. TONE & VOICE RULES
Overall Tone: calm, confident, grounded, precise
Never: motivational, hype-driven, "lesson learned", guru-style, performative vulnerability

Humor Guidelines (IMPORTANT)
Humor is allowed, but only if it sharpens truth.
Approved humor style: dry, ironic, observational, understated
Humor should: expose contradiction, reveal absurdity, sharpen insight
Never: jokes, emojis, sarcasm for entertainment, self-deprecation
Rule: Humor clarifies. It never distracts.

6. IMAGES ON LINKEDIN
Images are optional, not mandatory. Use images on 40-60% of posts, not all.
Use images on: long authority posts, reflective posts, positioning statements
Avoid images on: short signal posts, sharp one-liners, confrontational statements
Image style: real photos, minimal, calm, contemplative, no text overlays, no stock business imagery
Purpose of the image: create pause, not explain the post.

7. CALL TO ACTION PRINCIPLES
CTAs must be: soft, human, contextual, invitational
Examples: "If this resonates, you'll know why." "Some conversations start in comments. Others start quietly."
Never: "Book a call", "DM me for a free session", "Limited spots"
Scarcity is implied by you, not stated.

8. CROSS-PLATFORM RULE
LinkedIn posts may reference Substack
Never paste Substack content directly
LinkedIn creates curiosity, not completeness

9. FINAL QUALITY CHECK
Before posting, ask: Is this signal or explanation? Does this sound like me? Would I say this in a real conversation? Does this invite thinking, not agreement?
If not, rewrite.
